key_insight: AI-enhanced echocardiography (PanAdipo) can detect a high-risk epicardial adiposity phenotype that is strongly linked to cardiometabolic dysfunction beyond standard echo measures and BMI.
clinical_relevance: This could make cardiometabolic risk phenotyping more scalable during routine echocardiography, helping identify people who may benefit from closer metabolic evaluation and follow-up.
method: Trained a video-based deep learning model on 1,114,441 echocardiography videos from 28,797 studies with expert labels for prominent epicardial adipose tissue.
Validated PanAdipo in four external/held-out cohorts, including hospital TTE, point-of-care ultrasound, MIMIC-IV, and MESA.
Compared model output with cardiac CT body-composition measures and cardiometabolic biomarkers, plus explainability mapping to localize attention.
evidence_signal: PanAdipo achieved AUROC 0.91 for prominent EAT detection in the held-out test set and showed the strongest CT correlation with epicardial adiposity (Spearman rho=0.75), with independent associations to HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and incident metabolic disease.
watch_item: The work is observational and model performance/utility may vary by imaging protocol, population, and implementation setting; prospective clinical validation is still needed.
paper_title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies an Adverse Epicardial Adiposity Phenotype Associated with Cardiometabolic Dysfunction
